notes: Evaluate patterns top to bottom. The first pattern whose path is found (in order, across messages) decides the level. Then apply the floor and score thresholds. Stages inside a single message count in this order: TRUST, PRESSURE, ACCESS, EXPLOITATION.

patterns.name: full_attack_chain
patterns.reason: A trust claim was followed by a request to open or install something, and then by a request for secrets or money. This is the classic shape of a social-engineering attack.

patterns.name: pressure_to_exploitation
patterns.reason: A threat or time pressure was followed by a request for secrets or money. Attackers use pressure so people act before thinking.

patterns.name: access_to_exploitation
patterns.reason: The user was pushed to open a link, install an app or grant access, and then asked for secrets or money.

patterns.name: trust_to_critical_access
patterns.reason: A trust claim was followed by a request to install an app, open an installable file or grant sensitive access. This can give an attacker control of the device.

patterns.name: trust_to_secret_request
patterns.reason: An official-looking claim was followed by a request for an OTP or PIN. Genuine organisations never ask for these.

patterns.name: pressure_to_access
patterns.reason: Pressure was followed by a request to open a link or grant access. The pattern is concerning, but there is no request for secrets yet.

patterns.name: trust_to_pressure
patterns.reason: An official-looking claim was combined with pressure. This is common in the early stage of scams.

patterns.name: trust_to_access
patterns.reason: An official-looking claim was followed by a request to open a link. Check the sender through an official channel.

patterns.name: trust_to_exploitation
patterns.reason: A claim of authority or benefit was followed by a request for money or personal details.

floors.name: any_critical_signal
floors.reason: Contains a request that genuine services do not make: installing from outside a store, sensitive access, or a secret code.

scoreThresholds.note: Used when no pattern matched. Then the floor is applied.

HIGH.label: Potential social-engineering attack sequence detected
HIGH.uncertainty: This is an inference from the observed pattern. We cannot verify who the sender really is.
safeActions: Stop. Do not reply, click, install or share anything.
Contact the organisation only through its official website or app, not through details in these messages.
If you shared an OTP, PIN or money, call your bank immediately and report at cybercrime.gov.in or helpline 1930.
Share this warning with people who may receive the same messages.

SUSPICIOUS.label: Suspicious signals found
SUSPICIOUS.uncertainty: Some signals match scam patterns, but the evidence is not enough to be sure.
safeActions: Pause before acting on these messages.
Verify the sender through an official website, app or phone number you find yourself.
Do not share any OTP, PIN, password or card details.
If more messages arrive, add them here for a fuller check.

CANT_CONFIRM.label: Can't confirm
CANT_CONFIRM.uncertainty: There is not enough evidence to decide either way. This is not a confirmation that the messages are safe.
safeActions: Add any related earlier or later messages for a better assessment.
Verify the sender through an official channel if the message asks you to do anything.
Never share an OTP, PIN or password with anyone.

LOW.label: No known scam pattern found
LOW.uncertainty: BaitBreak found no known scam signals. This does not guarantee the messages are safe.
safeActions: Stay careful with any link or request you did not expect.
Never share an OTP, PIN or password with anyone.

safeActionsByRule.R12: Do not install any app sent through a message. Install apps only from the official Play Store or App Store.
safeActionsByRule.R13: Do not open or download the linked file.
safeActionsByRule.R14: Do not trust shortened links. Type the official website address yourself.
safeActionsByRule.R15: The link imitates a trusted website. Check the exact spelling and use the official site instead.
safeActionsByRule.R17: Never grant accessibility, screen-sharing or overlay permissions to an app you did not choose to install.
safeActionsByRule.R18: Do not install or open remote-access apps for someone who contacted you.
safeActionsByRule.R19: Never share an OTP with anyone, including people claiming to be from your bank or the government.
safeActionsByRule.R20: Never share your PIN, CVV or card details through a message or call.
safeActionsByRule.R21: Do not send money or pay fees to receive a benefit, prize or refund.
safeActionsByRule.R22: Do not share passwords or identity numbers through messages.
